standard_prerequisites: reduced induced closed subspace structures and scheme-theoretic unions of closed subspaces
properness, separatedness and quasi-compactness of morphisms of algebraic spaces and their permanence under closed immersions, compositions and images of universally closed maps
bijective closed immersions as universal homeomorphisms
core_obligations: Prove the equivalence of properness over Y for the reduced induced structure on T, for some closed subspace with support T, and for every closed subspace with support T
proof_roadmap: For (2) implies (3), take two closed subspace structures Z' and Z'' with support T, Z' proper over Y; the scheme-theoretic union Z''' is another closed subspace with the same support by the union description lemma
Z'' to Z''' is a closed immersion, so it suffices to prove Z''' to Y proper; Z' to Z''' is a bijective closed immersion, hence surjective and universally closed

Separatedness of Z''' to Y follows from separatedness of Z' to Y by the image lemma, local finite type from the immersion and composition lemmas, quasi-compactness from the universal homeomorphism, and universal closedness from the image-proper lemma, so Z''' to Y is proper
difficulty_reason: H2: a short structure-independence argument; the middle clause assembles five standard morphism lemmas, all quoted precisely.
